summary: Vincent Lefèvre works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the École Nationale des Chartes, completed his habilitation at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 2007 under Bruno Dagens, and served as a curator at the Guimet Museum.

Vincent Michaël Nicolaas Breugem is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned an MA (1996) and PhD (2012) from Leiden University, studied at Taisho, Kyoto, and Hanazono universities under Lucia Dolce, and was a Leiden research fellow in 2012.

Vincent Tournier specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and archaeology. Educated at the EPHE (PhD 2012) and Leiden under Cristina Scherrer-Schaub and Seishi Karashima, he has held posts at the EFEO, University of Tokyo, and Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Vincenzo Vergiani is an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Raffaele Torella from circa 1995 to 2001 and became Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Cambridge around 2010.

Indologist Vishnu Sitaram Sukthankar studied at St. Xavier's, St John's, Edinburgh, and Berlin (PhD 1921), working under Heinrich Lüders, Hermann Jacobi, and Moriz Winternitz. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India (1915–1919) and the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (1925).

Vishvanath Narayan Mandlik (1833–1899) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Elphinstone College (circa 1848–1852). He served as an examiner in Marathi and Law at the University of Mumbai and Vice-President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878).

Vishwa Nath Pathak (1926–2003) was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He held an academic post at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, serving as Professor there by 1987.

Vishwanath Prasad Varma (born 1924) works in philosophy, Indology, and history. He studied under Dhirendra Mohan Datta (~1942–1944), Ganga Nath Bhattacharya, doctoral supervisor Kali Kinkar Datta (~1947–1950), and Joachim Wach (1950).

Indologist Vishwanathan Venkatachalam studied at Madras, Nagpur, and Vikram universities. He served as Director of the Scindia Oriental Research Institute, Professor at Vikram University, and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University, among other leadership roles.

Vitus Angermeier is an Indologist who studied under Karin Preisendanz (completing his MA in 2007), Chlodwig H. Werba, and Roque Mesquita. By 2026, he was attested as a lecturer at the University of Vienna.

Vladimir Balabushevich (1900–1970) was an Indologist and historian. He served as Head of the Indian Department at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (attested in 1970 and 1990).

Vladimir Minorsky (1877–1966) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history. He studied law at Moscow Imperial University and at the Lazarev Institute of Oriental Languages, later holding academic posts at INALCO (~1923–1932) and SOAS University of London (~1932–1944).

Vladimir Tikhonov is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied at Saint Petersburg, Korea, and Moscow State universities under Mikhail Nikolaevich Pak, and later held posts at Kyung Hee University and the University of Oslo (Professor from 2006).

Volker Caumanns is a Tibetologist who earned an MA at Hamburg under David P. Jackson and a PhD at Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He has held teaching and research posts at Munich, Hamburg, Leipzig, Bern, and the Lumbini International Research Institute.

Volker Grabowsky works in Southeast Asian history and related fields. Educated at Kiel and Chiang Mai universities, he taught at Passau, Münster, and the National University of Laos, before becoming Chair of Thai Studies at the University of Hamburg in 2009.

Volker Zotz specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Vienna (1975–1986) and under Anagarika Govinda, later teaching at Vienna, Otani, Ryukoku, Saarland, and Luxembourg universities.
Vriti Sharma works in computational fields and Indology. She has held posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi and BharatGen.
W. F. Jayasuriya was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Rerukane Ariyaratne, H. D. Dharmasiriwardhana, and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.

W. H. R. Rivers (1864–1922) studied medicine at the University of London. He held clinical posts at several London hospitals, taught at Cambridge from 1893, became a Fellow of St John's College (1902), and served as president of the Anthropological Society.

W. Norman Brown (1892–1975) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield and Franklin Edgerton, he taught at Johns Hopkins and SPM Rajput College before serving as Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1926–1966).
